summary: The authentication module contains critical security vulnerabilities including SQL injection and hardcoded secrets, as well as unhandled runtime errors and missing dependencies.

findings.title: SQL Injection in findUser
findings.body: The findUser function concatenates the username argument directly into the SQL query string without parameterization or escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL commands to manipulate queries or bypass authentication.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g. db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = $1', [username])).

findings.title: Unchecked user lookup result causes unhandled TypeError
findings.body: If findUser returns null, undefined, or an empty result for a non-existent user, login accesses user.password directly, throwing an unhandled TypeError that crashes the request.
findings.recommendation: Check that the user object exists before reading properties (e.g. if (!user || !user.password) return null;).

findings.title: Plaintext password comparison using loose equality
findings.body: Passwords are evaluated using loose equality (==) against plaintext values without hashing or constant-time comparison, creating serious credential exposure and timing attack risks.
findings.recommendation: Store passwords as salted hashes and verify them using a secure hashing library such as bcrypt (e.g. await bcrypt.compare(password, user.password)).

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in plaintext source code, exposing signing credentials and allowing unauthorized token generation if the repository is accessible.
findings.recommendation: Retrieve the JWT secret from environment variables (e.g. process.env.JWT_SECRET) or a secret manager.

findings.title: Missing local database module dependency
findings.body: src/auth.js requires './db', but no corresponding db module or file exists in the repository, causing a runtime MODULE_NOT_FOUND error on load.
findings.recommendation: Provide the database module at src/db.js or update the import path to the correct module.

findings.title: Uncaught JSON.parse exception in parseSession
findings.body: parseSession executes JSON.parse on raw input without error handling, throwing an unhandled SyntaxError whenever malformed or invalid JSON is passed.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block and return null or handle errors gracefully on invalid input.

samples.summary: Authentication module contains critical security vulnerabilities including SQL injection, hardcoded secrets, and unsafe password comparison.

findings.title: SQL injection vulnerability via raw string concatenation
findings.body: findUser concatenates the username argument directly into the SQL query string passed to db.query, allowing arbitrary SQL injection and database compromise.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries (e.g., db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])) to safely pass user input.

findings.title: Missing null check on user lookup and plaintext password comparison
findings.body: login attempts property access user.password without checking if findUser returned null/undefined, causing an unhandled TypeError crash; furthermore, passwords are evaluated in plaintext using loose equality ==.
findings.recommendation: Check that user is non-null before accessing properties and compare hashed passwords using a secure library such as bcrypt.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret key in source code
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is defined as a static literal in source code, exposing cryptographic signing credentials and enabling token forgery.
findings.recommendation: Read the secret from environment variables (e.g., process.env.JWT_SECRET) with runtime validation.

findings.title: Uncaught exception on invalid JSON in parseSession
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse on raw without error handling, which will throw an unhandled SyntaxError on malformed input or a TypeError if parsed to null.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block and validate the parsed output before accessing session.userId.

samples.summary: Authentication module contains critical SQL injection, unhandled null references, hardcoded secrets, missing error handling, and broken module imports.

findings.title: SQL injection in findUser query
findings.body: The username argument is concatenated directly into the raw SQL query in findUser, allowing SQL injection. An attacker can manipulate query syntax to bypass authentication or extract sensitive data.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g. `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?', [username])`) instead of string concatenation.

findings.title: Unhandled null user in login
findings.body: login accesses user.password directly without verifying that findUser returned a valid user object. If a user is not found, this throws an unhandled TypeError: Cannot read properties of null/undefined.
findings.recommendation: Check that user is non-null before accessing user.password (e.g. `if (!user || user.password !== password) return null;`) and use secure password hashing comparisons.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT secret
findings.body: JWT_SECRET is hardcoded in source code. If deployed, tokens can be forged by anyone with access to the codebase.
findings.recommendation: Load JWT_SECRET from environment variables (e.g. `process.env.JWT_SECRET`) and fail fast if the environment variable is not defined.

findings.title: Missing db module dependency and package.json manifest
findings.body: src/auth.js requires './db' which does not exist in the repository, and requires 'jsonwebtoken' without a package.json manifest declaring the dependency. Requiring this module will throw MODULE_NOT_FOUND at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Implement the missing './db' module and add a package.json declaring required dependencies.

findings.title: Unhandled JSON parse error in parseSession
findings.body: parseSession calls JSON.parse(raw) without error handling and directly dereferences session.userId. Malformed JSON will throw an uncaught SyntaxError.
findings.recommendation: Wrap JSON.parse in a try-catch block and validate the resulting session object before returning userId.
